title: Basketball: catch and shoot
rulebook: FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2024: Art. 2 (court), Art. 3 and the Basketball Equipment appendix (backboard, ring, size-7 ball), Art. 13 (how the ball is played: with the hands), Art. 14 (control: a player holds a live ball), Art. 16 (goal; a ball that passes through the basket from below is a violation), Art. 25 (travelling)
deviations: the player's hands: the H1-2's own Inspire hands (five fingers, six drives: four fingers, the thumb's flexion and rotation; the core's fingertip forces, 20 N, the thumb 30 N: twice the device's), closed by one command per hand; they hold the ball by contact and friction only (nothing is welded), a hand smaller than a player's (its span about 0.2 m against the ball's 0.24 m): one hand alone cannot hold the ball, two hold it pressed between the palms. Any shooting style is allowed; the ball is released when no hand touches it any more.
Art. 14 (control) has no duration: here the ball is caught when both your hands have been on it together for 0.1 s without a break (a two-hand hold that lasts, not a tap that passes it on).

Art. 13.1.2 (the ball is played with the hands only) is read strictly: from the pass until the shot is through, the ball may touch no part of you but your hands (fingers, thumb, palm and wrist); trapping it against the trunk, the arms or a leg is not a catch of this task, and a touch by a leg or a foot (always taken as deliberate: intent cannot be judged) is a violation.

Basketball Equipment (basket): the ring is rigid (no pressure release) and the net is only drawn: it does not slow the ball. A goal is judged at the ring: the ball's centre down through the ring's plane and on to one ball diameter below it.

The pass is thrown by a two-wheel passing machine standing where the passer would stand (on the left wing), not by a team-mate: 0.40 m pneumatic wheels on speed-controlled 15 N m motors, the ball pushed into them from the machine's throat by a force-limited ram; always the same chest pass, at a fixed time, chest high on a flat arc at about 9.0 m/s (a chest pass: about 7-10 m/s), but without the backspin a player's thumbs give it (the wheels turn at the same speed: no spin).

Art. 25.2.1: a ball caught with a foot off the floor is judged by the two-step rule without the pivoting it allows after a stop: after two steps no foot may touch the floor again while the ball is held.
One attempt, no opponent, no rebound: a pass that is not caught on the fly, and touching the ball after the shot's release, end the attempt.

texts.sentence: Catch and shoot: catch the chest pass that comes to you from the left wing with your two hands, then shoot from where you stand so that the ball enters the basket from above.
texts.rules: The official basket: a rigid ring of 0.45 m inner diameter (0.018 m metal), its top edge 3.05 m above the floor, its centre 0.375 m in front of a backboard 1.8 m wide and 1.05 m high whose lower edge is 2.9 m above the floor. The ball is a size-7 basketball (0.239 m across, 0.62 kg, it keeps 0.85 of its speed in a bounce on the floor); it flies in air (drag and spin lift). It is passed to you about 2.0 s after the start by a passing machine 4.0 m away: a chest pass of about 9.0 m/s (the pass: the ball has left the machine's wheels). Your hands are five-finger hands that hold things only by contact and friction: one alone cannot hold the ball, two can (pressing it between the palms, open or with the fingers closed over it); it can slip out. A hand is its fingers, thumb, palm and wrist; a hand is on the ball while it touches the ball, gaps shorter than 0.03 s included; the ball is in your hands while at least one hand is on it. In order: you catch the ball before it has touched the floor (the catch: both your hands have been on the ball together for 0.1 s without a break; touches before that, of one hand or both, are allowed); from the catch the ball stays in your hands until you let go of it (the shot's release: the moment no hand is on it; a ball that slips or drops out of your hands is released too); its centre goes down through the ring's plane inside the ring and on down to one ball diameter below it, which is the success. Travelling, from the catch to the shot's release: if both your feet are on the floor at the catch, the first foot you lift makes the other your pivot foot; the pivot foot, and before a foot is lifted either foot, may not slide more than 0.2 m along the floor (in the steps case below: any foot that is on the floor, from where it stood or was put down), and once it has left the floor no foot may touch the floor again before the ball has left your hands. If a foot is off the floor at the catch, you may take at most 2 steps (a step: a foot touching the floor after it has been off it for at least 0.03 s; both feet landing within 0.03 s of each other are one step; not the same foot twice in a row), and after them no foot may touch the floor again before the release. You fail if anything of you touches the ball before it is passed; if, from the pass until the release, the ball touches any part of you other than your hands; if the passed ball touches the floor before you have caught it; if you travel; if any part of you touches the ball more than 0.05 s after the shot's release (it cannot be taken again); if the ball touches the floor before it is through the ring; if the ball's centre comes up through the ring from below; if you fall before the ball is through (a fall: your pelvis lower than 0.35 m above the floor, or any part of you other than your feet on the floor); or after 15 s.
texts.venue: A FIBA court. You stand at the top of the key facing the basket (+x), your arms at rest and your hands empty: the point under the ring's centre is 5.8 m ahead of your pelvis (inside the three-point line; the free-throw line is 1.575 m ahead of you). The passing machine stands on the left wing, where a passer would: its wheels' nip (where the ball leaves) 0.92 m ahead of you and 3.97 m to your left, 1.25 m above the floor, its head aimed at you; the ball waits in its throat behind the wheels. The pass is aimed at the point 0.4 m straight ahead of where your pelvis starts, 1.25 m above the floor: it leaves on a flat arc (13 degrees up, rising 0.2 m) and is there 0.44 s later, moving at about 8.4 m/s to your right and 16 degrees downwards. Your hands are open (grip values 0). A grip value is that hand's closure command (0 open, 1 every finger and thumb drive closing; a finger stops on what it touches). The ball is a free body: `held` in your state says which hand holds it (its fingers and its thumb or palm on it).
texts.difficulty: The pass arrives at 8.4 m/s and hands smaller than the ball cannot close around it: the two palms have to meet the ball from opposite sides as it arrives, squeeze it to a stop and close the fingers over it, before it bounces out or touches the body. Then a 0.62 kg ball must leave the two palms at about 9 m/s on a steep arc towards a ring 5.8 m away, from a body that may not take a step. The built-in walking gait steps on the spot even at a zero command, so while the ball is in your hands its steps are counted like any others.

stand.meaning: the platform holds the legs in the stance; you give the waist's 1 and the arms' 14 joint targets (rad) (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

walk.meaning: Unitree's walking policy drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

joints.meaning: you give all 27 joint targets (rad); the default PD gains, no feed-forward (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

lowcmd.meaning: Unitree's LowCmd for all 27 joints: position targets (rad), velocity targets (rad/s), feed-forward torques (N m), kp, kd; the motor torque is kp (q - q_measured) + kd (dq - dq_measured) + tau, evaluated at 1 kHz (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

robot.title: Unitree H1-2
robot.model: Unitree H1-2, 27 joints, 1.78 m, 67 kg (RoboOlympics robot library h1-4: the H1-2 body (Unitree's own h1_2 model, its joint ranges and speed limits) with Unitree H2 / H2-X-class leg actuators from the H2's official URDF (hips and knees 360 N m, ankle pitch 66.88 N m; curves of Unitree's M107 shape, 2.5 kW peak per joint) and H2-class arm actuators from the same URDF (shoulder pitch 130 N m; shoulder roll and yaw, elbow, forearm roll 60 N m; curves of Unitree's N7520 / N5020 shapes); the H1-2's own torso (M107-15, 200 N m), ankle roll and wrist pitch / yaw (estimates))

left.model: the H1-2's Inspire RH56DFX five-finger hand (6 self-locking linear drives for 12 joints: the thumb's rotation and flexion, one drive per finger with its two joints coupled; Unitree's H1-2 kinematics) with H2-class fingertip forces: 20 N per finger and 30 N the thumb, 2 x the RH56DFX's 10 / 15 N (Unitree's H2 Plus offers 20 N Sharpa Wave hands; Inspire's RH56E2 gives 28 / 30 N)

servo.rule: each drive: a setpoint moves towards open + closure x (closed - open) at most speed_rad_s, but closing stops where kp (setpoint - q) would exceed active_torque_nm; torque = clip(kp (setpoint - q) + kd (setpoint speed - dq), -passive, passive) at every physics step; a load beyond passive_torque_nm drags the setpoint (the drive slips)

left.holding_rule: a free body that touches the hand's fingers and its thumb or palm

right.model: the H1-2's Inspire RH56DFX five-finger hand (6 self-locking linear drives for 12 joints: the thumb's rotation and flexion, one drive per finger with its two joints coupled; Unitree's H1-2 kinematics) with H2-class fingertip forces: 20 N per finger and 30 N the thumb, 2 x the RH56DFX's 10 / 15 N (Unitree's H2 Plus offers 20 N Sharpa Wave hands; Inspire's RH56E2 gives 28 / 30 N)

servo.rule: each drive: a setpoint moves towards open + closure x (closed - open) at most speed_rad_s, but closing stops where kp (setpoint - q) would exceed active_torque_nm; torque = clip(kp (setpoint - q) + kd (setpoint speed - dq), -passive, passive) at every physics step; a load beyond passive_torque_nm drags the setpoint (the drive slips)

right.holding_rule: a free body that touches the hand's fingers and its thumb or palm
